blocks.text: 并行主义。 许多现实世界的任务会分解成独立的子任务， 可以同时执行。需要文献审查，数据分析和报告撰写的研究管道可以同时运行所有三个，大幅缩短墙时钟时间。序列单剂处理是多剂并行主义消除的瓶颈。
blocks.originalExcerpt: Parallelism. Many real-world tasks decompose into independent sub-tasks that can be executed concurrently. A research pipeline that requires literature review, data analysis, and report writing can run all three in parallel, dramatically reducing wall-clock time. Sequential single-agent processing is a bottleneck that multi-agent parallelism eliminates.

blocks.text: 强力。 单剂是失败的单一点。 如果它产生幻觉， 被卡在环中， 或产生一个隐蔽错误的答案， 则没有检查。多剂系统引入冗余:第二剂可以验证、批评或独立地重新确定结果。 反面剂可以在相信输出之前对弱点进行探究。
blocks.originalExcerpt: Robustness. A single agent is a single point of failure. If it hallucinates, gets stuck in a loop, or produces a subtly wrong answer, there is no check. Multi-agent systems introduce redundancy: a second agent can verify, critique, or independently re-derive results. Adversarial agents can probe for weaknesses before outputs are trusted.

blocks.originalExcerpt: The topology of a multi-agent system—how agents are connected and how authority flows among them—is the most consequential architectural decision. Four canonical patterns have emerged, each with distinct trade-offs.

blocks.title: 编者阅读提示
blocks.text: 阅读 §25.2.1「Centralized (Supervisor/Manager) Architecture」 时，先按“输入—状态—控制流—输出”还原原书描述，再追踪每个组件由谁执行、数据写到哪里、失败会怎样向下游传播。这样可以避免只记住组件名称，却无法解释完整运行路径。
在中央架构中，一个单一的管弦乐团Agent(不同意义上的主管，经理，或规划者)掌握着全球状态，分解任务，将子任务分配给工人Agent，并汇总其成果。地貌是一个枢纽式的和声:所有通信都通过中央节点流。
blocks.originalExcerpt: In a centralized architecture, a single orchestrator agent (variously called supervisor, manager, or planner) holds global state, decomposes tasks, delegates sub-tasks to worker agents, and aggregates their results. The topology is a hub-and-spoke: all communication flows through the central node.

blocks.text: 集中式建筑权衡方案:简单控制流程;明确问责;易于调试(所有决定都放在一个地方);直接执行。
blocks.originalExcerpt: Centralized Architecture Trade-offs Pros: Simple control flow; clear accountability; easy to debug (all decisions in one place); straightforward to implement.

blocks.text: 康斯:失败的单一点——如果管理者产生幻觉或感到困惑，整个系统都会失败;管理者在高负荷下成为瓶颈;管理者context window必须持有全局状态，限制可扩展性。

blocks.text: 阅读 §25.2.2「Decentralized (Peer-to-Peer) Architecture」 时，先按“输入—状态—控制流—输出”还原原书描述，再追踪每个组件由谁执行、数据写到哪里、失败会怎样向下游传播。这样可以避免只记住组件名称，却无法解释完整运行路径。
在分散的架构中， Agent在没有中央协调器的情况下直接相互交流。地形学是网格:任何Agent都可以与任何其他人交流。协调产生于地方互动而不是全球规划。
blocks.originalExcerpt: In a decentralized architecture, agents interact directly with one another without a central coordinator. The topology is a mesh: any agent can communicate with any other. Coordination emerges from local interactions rather than global planning. Emergent coordination in peer-to-peer systems arises through mechanisms such as:

blocks.text: • 谈判:Agent竞价执行任务或资源
blocks.originalExcerpt: • Negotiation: agents bid for tasks or resources

blocks.text: • 污名:Agent修改他人观察到的共用状态(见第25.3.6节)

blocks.text: • 地方共识:少数机构在没有全球协调的情况下达成协议
blocks.originalExcerpt: • Local consensus: small groups of agents reach agreement without global coordination

blocks.text: 分散式建筑权衡:对个别Agent失败具有弹性;自然增加Agent的尺度;没有瓶颈。
blocks.originalExcerpt: Decentralized Architecture Trade-offs Pros: Resilient to individual agent failures; scales naturally as agents are added; no bottleneck.

blocks.text: 康斯:很难调试-紧急行为难以追踪;当Agent对状态的看法不一致时，可能会发生冲突;协调的间接费用随着O(n2)的天真消息传来而增加;难以保证全球的一致性。
blocks.originalExcerpt: Cons: Hard to debug—emergent behavior is difficult to trace; potential for conflicts when agents have inconsistent views of state; coordination overhead grows as O(n2 ) with naive message passing; difficult to guarantee global consistency.

等级结构将集中式模式概括为具有多层次管理功能的树结构，顶级管弦乐代表到特定域的子管理者，而子管理者则委托给专业工人。这反映了大型企业的组织结构。
blocks.originalExcerpt: Hierarchical architectures generalize the centralized pattern into a tree structure with multiple levels of management. A top-level orchestrator delegates to domain-specific sub-managers, who in turn delegate to specialized workers. This mirrors the organizational structure of large enterprises. Key features of hierarchical systems:

blocks.text: • 权力下放链:权力和背景流经树下;结果向上流动
blocks.originalExcerpt: • Delegation chains: authority and context flow down the tree; results flow up

blocks.text: • 升级途径:工人可以将无法解决的问题升级到管理人员手中
blocks.originalExcerpt: • Escalation paths: workers can escalate unresolvable issues to their manager

blocks.text: • 域隔离:子管理者保持特定域的背景，减少认知
blocks.originalExcerpt: • Domain isolation: sub-managers maintain domain-specific context, reducing the cognitive

blocks.originalExcerpt: The enterprise analogy is apt: a CEO (top orchestrator) sets strategy; VPs (sub-managers) translate strategy into domain plans; individual contributors (workers) execute. The hierarchy enables scale while preserving accountability.

市场机制通过拍卖和投标分配任务和资源。
blocks.originalExcerpt: Market mechanisms allocate tasks and resources through auctions and bidding. The Contract Net Protocol [334], one of the oldest multi-agent coordination mechanisms, is a task auction:

blocks.text: 1. 管理人员播放附有要求的任务通知
blocks.originalExcerpt: 1. A manager broadcasts a task announcement with requirements

blocks.text: 2. 承包商Agent提交投标(能力申报+费用估计数)
blocks.originalExcerpt: 2. Contractor agents submit bids (capability declarations + cost estimates)

blocks.text: 3. 经理将合同授予最有竞争力的投标人
blocks.originalExcerpt: 3. The manager awards the contract to the best bidder

blocks.text: 4. 中标的承包商执行并报告结果
blocks.originalExcerpt: 4. The winning contractor executes and reports results

blocks.text: 在LLM系统中，投标可以用自然语言(“我能够以高度自信的3步完成”)或结构化格式表示。市场机制对于必须尽量减少API成本的受资源限制环境特别有效。
blocks.originalExcerpt: In LLM systems, bids can be expressed in natural language (“I can complete this in 3 steps with high confidence”) or structured formats. Market mechanisms are particularly effective for resource-constrained settings where API costs must be minimized.

blocks.originalExcerpt: Stigmergy [117] replaces explicit agent-to-agent messaging with a simpler mechanism: each agent modifies the shared environment as a side effect of its work, and other agents react to those modifications rather than to direct signals. The classic illustration is a foraging ant depositing pheromone on its return path; subsequent ants amplify successful routes...
